replacements.old: Identify the Hermitian bispinor momentum matrix by $T_{\alpha\dot\beta}=\sigma^\mu_{\alpha\dot\beta}P_\mu$, where $P_\mu=\eta_{\mu\nu}P^\nu$. This fixes the mixed relation as $\{Q^I_\alpha,\bar Q_{\dot\beta J}\}=-2\sigma^\mu_{\alpha\dot\beta}P_\mu\delta^I{}_J$.
replacements.new: Define abstract translation coordinates $p_0=(T_{1\dot1}+T_{2\dot2})/2$, $p_1=(T_{1\dot2}+T_{2\dot1})/2$, $p_2=(T_{2\dot1}-T_{1\dot2})/(2i)$, and $p_3=(T_{1\dot1}-T_{2\dot2})/2$. Then $T_{\alpha\dot\beta}=\sigma^\mu_{\alpha\dot\beta}p_\mu$, $p_\mu^*=p_\mu$, and $\tau(ip_\mu)=ip_\mu$. A representation of the complex supertranslation algebra $\mathfrak t=V\oplus C_N\oplus\mathfrak g_{\bar1}$ on a graded complex vector space $\mathcal D$ means a parity-preserving complex-linear map $\rho:\mathfrak t\to\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(\mathcal D)$ preserving the bracket, where the target bracket is the operator supercommutator. Write $P_\mu=\rho(p_\mu)$ and use the charge symbols for their images. Thus $\rho(T_{\alpha\dot\beta})=\sigma^\mu_{\alpha\dot\beta}P_\mu$ and the represented mixed relation is $\{Q^I_\alpha,\bar Q_{\dot\beta J}\}=-2\sigma^\mu_{\alpha\dot\beta}P_\mu\delta^I{}_J$, with $P_\mu=\eta_{\mu\nu}P^\nu$. In a unitary realization the images $P_\mu$ are restrictions of the self-adjoint physical momenta to their common invariant domain; $\rho(ip_\mu)=iP_\mu$, so $-i\rho(ip_\mu)=P_\mu$.

replacements.old: The domain $\mathcal D$ is invariant under those generators and under $U(\mathcal P)$.
replacements.new: The domain $\mathcal D$ is invariant under those generators and under $U(\mathcal P)$. Explicitly, these restrictions define the complex-linear supertranslation representation $\rho_{\mathcal D}:\mathfrak t\to\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(\mathcal D)$: it sends the abstract $p_\mu$ to $P_\mu|_{\mathcal D}$ and each abstract supercharge or central generator to its named operator restricted to $\mathcal D$. Invariance of $\mathcal D$ makes these endomorphisms, and the assumed bracket identities make $\rho_{\mathcal D}$ bracket-preserving. In particular, $\rho_{\mathcal D}(T_{\alpha\dot\beta})=\sigma^\mu_{\alpha\dot\beta}P_\mu|_{\mathcal D}$ and $-i\rho_{\mathcal D}(ip_\mu)=P_\mu|_{\mathcal D}$.
